pr_title: Allow dynamic port allocation for hdfs fixture
pr_body:
Running multiple hdfs fixtures in parallel for running integration tests requires
a dynamic port assignment in order to avoid port clashes. This introduces
the ability to assign port ranges to gradle projects that can be used
to allocate dynamically ports used by these projects.

We apply this dynamic port setup for hdfs fixtures used in
`:x-pack:plugin:searchable-snapshots:qa `only at the moment as
tests sources (rest tests) in `:plugins:repository-hdfs` still rely on
hard coded ports.

This is a simplified version of fixtures I created before on the gradle codebase 
to deal with similar issues.

Fixes #66377
pr_comments: Merging to unblock others from CI failures.

issue_context.title: Build fails to start hdfsFixture due to port conflict
issue_context.body:
We've started getting a number of build failures bringing up test fixtures.

https://gradle-enterprise.elastic.co/scans/failures?failures.failureClassification=all_failures&failures.failureMessage=Execution%20failed%20for%20task%20*%0A%3E%20Failed%20to%20start%20*&search.relativeStartTime=P7D&search.timeZoneId=America/Los_Angeles

It seems the root cause is that the port (`9999` in this case) seems to be already in use:
```
java.net.BindException: Problem binding to [localhost:9999] java.net.BindException: Address already in use; For more details see:  http://wiki.apache.org/hadoop/BindException
```

The most likely explanation is that there is another instance of this fixture in use at the time. Given the timing, it seems likely that #65832 might be related to this. I'm not sure what logic was in place before to ensure this scenario didn't happen but it looks like we either a) aren't managing parallelism for fixtures like we did before or b) aren't shutting down previous instances as aggressively as we used to.
comments: @breskeby do you mind taking a look at this?

Will do. I did changes in that area. Wonder if that might be related.

On Tue 15. Dec 2020 at 17:33, Mark Vieira <notifications@github.com> wrote:

> @breskeby <https://github.com/breskeby> do you mind taking a look at this?

I can reproduce it locally via `./gradlew :plugins:repository-hdfs:check :x-pack:plugin:searchable-snapshots:qa:hdfs:check`

I think the timing of the stop fixture task execution is causing this. The former wiring didn't guarantee running them in the "right" order neither ( finalizedBy task are not guaranteed to be executed immediately) but the actual implementation made a difference here. Will look for a more robust solution here. Worst case we can wire the previous task order manually

Thanks Rene, if we can't come up with a solution quickly we might need to revert these changes. We've had over 100 builds fail due to this just since yesterday so it's a pretty common occurrence even if the previous implementation only worked incidentally.

https://gradle-enterprise.elastic.co/scans/failures?failures.failureClassification=all_failures&failures.failureMessage=Execution%20failed%20for%20task%20*%0A%3E%20Failed%20to%20start%20hdfsFixture&search.relativeStartTime=P7D&search.timeZoneId=America/Los_Angeles

As said, how it was done before wasn't bulletproof either. I went ahead and introduced the possibility of dynamically setting the port on these fixtures. This should be a more robust solution and also allow us to run these tests in parallel. There was even an older todo on this: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/bf5866048262d897ede629293b6fe26c3b108b7a/test/fixtures/hdfs-fixture/src/main/java/hdfs/MiniHDFS.java#L101

the PR with a fix is here: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/66440

review_comments: What's the motivation for having these port ranges per-project? Why not just allocate a single big block for the entire build?
I remember we introduced these ranges in gradle too, to make debugging this a bit easier. I don't have hard feelings or strong opinions here. I like the separation between projects though.
From what I can tell `assignePort` and `releasePort` are never used. Is there something that needs to be still wired up?
kind of an oversight. I remove this as it's not used at the moment
